question: According to the original Petersdorf-Beeson (1961) definition, which combination of criteria is required to classify a fever as classic Fever of Unknown Origin (FUO)?

answers.text: Temperature >38.0°C on two or more occasions for ≥2 weeks, undiagnosed after routine outpatient evaluation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The temperature threshold is >38.3°C (not >38.0°C) and the duration is ≥3 weeks (not 2 weeks).

answers.text: Temperature >38.3°C on several occasions for ≥3 weeks, undiagnosed after 1 week of in-hospital investigation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Temperature >38.3°C, duration ≥3 weeks, and remaining undiagnosed after ≥1 week of in-hospital evaluation are the three defining criteria.

answers.text: Temperature >38.3°C for ≥2 weeks, undiagnosed after two outpatient visits

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The required duration is ≥3 weeks, and diagnosis must remain elusive after structured in-hospital investigation — not merely outpatient visits.

answers.text: Temperature >39.0°C on any occasion for ≥1 week, with negative blood cultures and CXR

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The threshold is >38.3°C (not >39.0°C), duration is ≥3 weeks, and the undiagnosed criterion is after systematic in-hospital work-up — not two specific negative tests.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Petersdorf-Beeson triad: >38.3°C + ≥3 weeks duration + undiagnosed after ≥1 week of systematic in-hospital investigation.
Excellent. Remembering the three numbers — 38.3°C, 3 weeks, 1 week in-hospital — is the foundation for all FUO reasoning.
